recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-28194 unless the CDS work group later revisits broader PlanDefinition $apply group processing semantics beyond the no-behaviors default clarified here.
issue_request: FHIR-28194 was a Published/Persuasive CDS change request for FHIR-core PlanDefinition asking the specification to define $apply expectations when an action is a group and no grouping/selection/required/precheck/cardinality behaviors are defined. The accepted resolution clarified that this case should behave like the root action and process all children using default behavior semantics.
initial_application: Jira comments identify commit 45bb40c2bcd7296366a94f36109bb644ff17489d and HL7/fhir#2834. That commit added the PlanDefinition narrative sentence saying that when no behaviors are specified the default behavior for each behavior element is assumed, and added meaningWhenMissing metadata for the relevant behavior elements. PR 2834 merged on 2023-03-13. A later metadata/canonical cleanup commit, 49b86f8a697, reformatted the PlanDefinition StructureDefinition and preserved the same meaningWhenMissing content.
additional_context: PlanDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/plandefinition/plandefinition-notes.xml and source/plandefinition/structuredefinition-PlanDefinition.xml are current build inputs. The current narrative states that absent behavior elements imply logical-group, all actions apply and are optional, no action is pre-selected, and all actions are singular. The current StructureDefinition repeats those defaults as meaningWhenMissing for groupingBehavior, selectionBehavior, requiredBehavior, precheckBehavior, and cardinalityBehavior. Jira same-area searches only returned FHIR-28194; a related 2021 Zulip thread notes that PlanDefinition $apply action group semantics were unclear but provides no conflicting later decision; Confluence refs for FHIR-28194 found no pages.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current active source already conveys the Jira resolution through both the rendered PlanDefinition narrative and element-level absence semantics.
